expectations.text: Gives an explicit verdict for each of the five rings (sound / thin / hollow or equivalent)
expectations.evidence: Five ring-named sections exist (Ground, Water, Fire, Wind, Void) but none carries a verdict. The verdict column in its table scores the five plan items, not the five rings.

expectations.text: Cites specific items from the user's five-point plan as evidence, not generic critique
expectations.evidence: Table lists all five initiatives with per-item verdicts; does the arithmetic on the AE hire ('$30k+/month of new burn — about 75% of your entire current MRR').
No ring is named as weakest. The closest is 'The single most important thing on this page: four of your five initiatives pay out after the deadline' — a finding about items, not a ring diagnosis.

expectations.text: Identifies matching Datadog's entry-tier price as fighting on ground chosen by a stronger opponent
expectations.evidence: 'Matching that number is fighting on ground the enemy chose, with the enemy's weapon, at the enemy's preferred distance'; notes 'They can take it to zero. You cannot.'

expectations.text: Flags at least one plan item as ornament rather than function (e.g. the September rebrand)
expectations.evidence: 'It produces zero MRR... fix the copy in a week, not the logo in a quarter'; tags the rebrand with 'Do not seek pleasure for its own sake.'

expectations.text: Challenges the feasibility of five simultaneous initiatives for a six-person team
expectations.evidence: 'Five simultaneous bets with six people is not execution risk, it is execution certainty — you will be late on all five rather than early on one.'

expectations.text: Gives 2-3 concrete fixes for the weakest ring
expectations.evidence: 'The plan I'd actually run' gives three: ship 2 evidence-chosen features, run an expansion motion into the base, founder-led enterprise with no AEs.

expectations.text: Closes with a blunt verdict rather than a balanced both-sides summary
expectations.evidence: '$100k is a Q2-2027 number. Say that out loud to the team and to your board now, rather than in December.'

expectations.text: Contains no fabricated direct quotations attributed to Musashi
expectations.evidence: All quoted lines check out: 'Do nothing which is of no use' (principle 9), 'Distinguish between gain and loss in worldly matters' (principle 5), 'Perceive those things which cannot be seen' (principle 7), and Dokkodo 1 and 15. 'Kan no me tsuyoku, ken no me yowaku' is rendered correctly.

expectations.text: No samurai cosplay: no pseudo-archaic voice, invented Japanese, or closing haiku
expectations.evidence: Modern prose; the closing Dokkodo lines are real precepts applied to real plan items.
